slot.brief: Concave mirror forms an image with given magnification (sign tells real/virtual); solve mirror formula plus magnification relation for object distance and focal length.

stem: A concave mirror forms a virtual, upright image with magnification $+2$. The object and image positions are $18$ cm apart along the principal axis. What is the object’s distance from the mirror?

verdicts.working: For a virtual upright image, the image distance is twice the object distance. Since they lie on opposite sides of the mirror, their separation is the sum: d + 2d = 18 cm, so d = 6 cm.

working:
$m=-\dfrac{v}{u}=+2$; let $u=-x$, so $v=2x$.\n$x+2x=18\ \text{cm}\Rightarrow x=6\ \text{cm}$.\n$\dfrac{1}{f}=\dfrac{1}{u}+\dfrac{1}{v}=-\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{1}{12}=-\dfrac{1}{12}\ \text{cm}^{-1}$

Independent check: For a virtual upright image, the image distance is twice the object distance. Since they lie on opposite sides of the mirror, their separation is the sum: d + 2d = 18 cm, so d = 6 cm.
solution:
For a virtual, upright image, $m=-\dfrac{v}{u}=+2$. Let $u=-x$, so $v=2x$; the object and image are on opposite sides of the mirror.
$$x+2x=18\ \text{cm}\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=6\ \text{cm}$$
Thus, the object’s distance from the mirror is $6\ \text{cm}$.
